rationale: X has a distinctive editorial serif voice, a specific hero product card (staff, keyboard, practice streak, mock exam score) and a cohesive green, cream and terracotta palette with a strong dark stats band. Y is clean but follows the centred-hero plus browser-frame timetable pattern, with bright orange and generic clip-art feature illustrations, so it reads more template-like. X's mobile page is very long, but both are competent there.

Y has a distinctive hero product card (staff, piano keys, practice streak, mock exam score), a confident serif display type, a cohesive green, cream and gold palette, and well-paced sections ending in a strong dark footer. X is competent but centred, template-like: a flat timetable grid as its hero visual, a repeated card layout and weaker contrast between sections. Y is the one a design director would ship.

Y has a bolder, confident serif headline, a richer plum/pink/apricot palette, a specific hero scene with picked-at and delivery chips, and a stronger closing CTA with a real offer. X is clean and has nice feature illustrations, but its hero card has a dead empty lower area, small tilted chips and a sparse, more uniform card-grid rhythm that reads more template-like.

X has a confident oversized serif headline, a warm plum and blush palette with a deep purple band, and specific copy and data (picked at 7am, delivery window chips) that feel wild and generous. Y has richer feature illustrations but a hero card with an awkward empty strip, and its card grids and layout read as a more standard SaaS template.

X has a confident editorial serif headline, a strong deep-green/amber palette, and specific GBP product cards (balance, deposit progress, loan offer) with distinctive feature illustrations. Y is clean and its app-window hero is convincing, but the beige/green palette, stacked logo strip with mixed fonts, wrapped hero text and generic feature tiles feel more like a standard SaaS template. X's hero card overlap and a very long mobile page are minor flaws, but X is the one a design director would ship.

Y has a stronger serif headline, a confident green/amber/rust palette, and a clearer hero with layered account, goal and loan cards plus specific feature mini-UIs. X has a nice round-up app window in its hero, but its feature illustrations are abstract blob patterns and the overall layout is a more familiar cream-and-green SaaS template. X's hero is also slightly cramped, with the logo strip cut at the fold. Y reads as more ship-ready and distinctive.

Y has a bolder, more deliberate identity: a dark-green product window with waveform and listener card, a strong serif display, and dark bands that give the page rhythm. X is clean and its hero UI is specific, but the cream and terracotta card grid, the weaker spacing and the large empty gaps read as a more standard template. Y's feature illustrations and pricing are also more cohesive.

X has a strong editorial serif display type, a deep green and cream palette with a coral accent, and a dark product mockup with a waveform and directory status list, which together give it a distinctive, ship-ready look. Y has a good hero UI with specific copy and per-feature illustrations, but its pale cards, pink band and sans body type follow the familiar SaaS layout, and its grey empty areas (the hero's lower half and the Pro pricing column) feel less finished. X is the one a design director would ship, and Y is the more template-like of the two.
